meta.title: FORGE — BJJ / Judo / Wrestling / Sanda Strength & Power Library
equipment_allowed: Bumper Plates / Lifting Platform (for Olympic-lift variants)

Novice.grip_work: Submaximal — build tissue tolerance, no max hangs/holds to failure
Novice.notes: Goal is owning the squat/hinge/press/pull pattern and building base tissue tolerance (neck, grip, low back) before any max-effort work. No barbell work above 65% e1RM.

Beginner.grip_work: Timed holds submaximal (60-70% of max hang time)
Beginner.notes: Add posterior-chain and grip volume — this is where most durability for grappling gets built. Trap bar and safety bar enter rotation to reduce spinal load while loading the pattern.

Intermediate.intensity_power: Moderate-heavy, contrast pairing with a strength lift
Intermediate.grip_work: Max-effort timed holds 1x/week, submaximal the rest
Intermediate.notes: Strength-power split begins. Contrast method (heavy pull/press followed by explosive med-ball or trap-bar jump) enters rotation to build transferable power for throws/scrambles.

Advanced.grip_work: Max hangs/holds programmed like a main lift, tracked for progression
Advanced.notes: Camp periodization required (GPP -> SPP -> Peak -> Taper). Heavy pulling/hinging kept 48-72h from live randori/sparring/wrestling days. Reverse hyper used as both posterior-chain builder and spinal decompression/recovery tool.

Elite.intensity_main: 85-97% e1RM, RPE 8-10 only in peak block
Elite.intensity_power: Max intent, autoregulated by bar speed
Elite.grip_work: Fully individualized — programmed off actual grip fatigue data from the mat/circle
Elite.notes: S&C is fully subordinate to the competition calendar. Everything is built backward from weigh-in and first match. Load is set by daily readiness, not the written number on the page.

sport_emphasis.BJJ: Grip endurance and isometric strength (holding position) matter more than peak power — bias sets/reps toward controlled tempo and longer time-under-tension on pulls and carries.
sport_emphasis.Judo: Explosive hip extension and pulling power (for kuzushi/throws) are the priority — bias toward the Power/Explosive split and trap-bar/KB jump work.
sport_emphasis.Wrestling: Repeated explosive efforts (shots, sprawls, scrambles) — bias toward contrast pairing (heavy hinge/squat + explosive throw_power movement) and conditioning_simple complexes.
sport_emphasis.Sanda: Blend of striking (from the earlier striking file) and clinch/throw ability — this file's grappling side should pair with the sport's striking S&C, emphasizing grip, neck and hip power for clinch entries and throws.

global_rules: Full commercial gym on-site — all barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell, cable/machine, and conditioning equipment listed above is available without restriction; no equipment constraint applies to any template in this library.
Every session follows this order: throw_power/explosive work first -> main strength lift (squat/hinge/press/pull) -> grip/neck/core accessory last. Never lift heavy after grinding grip work.

Reverse Hyper is used two ways: as a posterior-chain strength builder (loaded, 8-12 reps) on strength days, and as a light spinal-decompression recovery tool (bodyweight pendulum, high reps) the day after live sparring/randori/wrestling.

Weighted Dip Belt is the only added-load tool for pull-ups/dips — keeps the exercise pool simple; progress load in small increments (2.5-5kg) once bodyweight reps hit the top of the rep range for 2 sessions running.
Heavy squat/hinge/pull days are placed 48h+ from live randori, sparring, or wrestling practice wherever the schedule allows.
Grip and neck work is always programmed at the end of the session, regardless of level — pre-fatiguing grip ruins every pulling and clinch-relevant lift that follows.
Deload every 4th week at 40-50% volume reduction for Intermediate and above; Novice/Beginner deload by simply repeating the lightest week of the block.
Novice and Beginner never train above 65-75% e1RM on any barbell lift — priority is pattern ownership and tissue tolerance (especially neck and grip) before load.

Contrast pairing (heavy strength lift immediately followed by an explosive throw_power movement, full recovery between) is the main power-development tool from Intermediate level up — it is the single best return for grapplers on this equipment list.

Olympic-lift variants (hang power clean, power clean, push jerk, KB snatch) are included for their hip-extension power transfer to throws/shots, but are Intermediate-level-and-up only — Novice/Beginner athletes train the same power quality through trap-bar jumps, KB swings, and med-ball throws until the lift technique itself has been coached and grooved separately.
Competition week: strength work stops 5-6 days out; only light trap-bar jumps or med-ball throws (low volume, high quality) remain up to 2-3 days out for CNS priming, then full rest.
